title: Doug King on Commodities, Risk Control & the Illusion of Trends - Open Interest - Ep.20

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Doug King on Commodities, Risk Control & the Illusion of Trends - Open Interest - Ep.20.docx

speakers: Doug King (founder, Merchant Commodity Fund; former Cargill head of petroleum trading)
Moritz Seibert (host, Open Interest; caption 'Morett Sebert')
summary: Open Interest ep.20 (Dec 2025): discretionary commodity fund manager on bottom-up supply and demand trading, cash-versus-futures signals and risk control. Conclusions: commodities are cyclical because of innovation, avoid passive index, rely on basis and physical data, and use volatility targeting with drawdown cuts.

coverage.note: intro, host bio of Doug King, football chat; teaser repeated in C06
career path, start of Merchant Commodity Fund, discretionary bottom-up approach
cash vs futures, commodity universe, team size, commodity cycles and innovation (shale)
shale, GMO, electrification, passive commodity ETFs
rocket-ship moments, concentration limits, drawdown rules, vol target
volatility targeting limits, real vs not real moves, margin squeezes
exchange limits, flat price vs curve trades, relative value, start of 2014 oil trade
LME nickel aftermath, RCMA physical business
physical info, basis, filtering noise, copper example
hardest part of money management: de-risking, recruitment and hedge fund structure

completeness_estimate: 0.92 - first reader captured nearly all of King's methods, risk process, trades and numbers; missed a few secondary points (hedger margin-call risk, LNG decoupling, exchange bail-out, pod-shop leash) and merged two speakers in one claim.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we're very bottom up focused. Uh we we go and do the you know the supply and demand work
claims.claim: The fund is discretionary and bottom-up: supply and demand analysis for each commodity, with optimisation and timing tools only for execution.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we felt that fundamental trading and you know looking at commodities as a as a merchant would rather than anyone else would be advantageous at that point
claims.claim: A merchant's fundamental view gave an edge in 2004 when Asia was booming and few vehicles offered commodity exposure.
claims.conditions: 2004 commodity boom with few competing funds

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: a futures derivative price and a a cash market price can diverge um you know giving different signals
claims.claim: Divergence between futures and the cash market gives conviction signals, so cash information is checked before a futures view is traded.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: We do commodities that are really impacted by fundamental um supply and demand global movement and substitution arbitrage that type of thing
claims.claim: The universe is oil, gas, industrial metals and softs, excluding precious metals, which are not driven by physical supply and demand.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we may not trade those or any of those sectors for you know long periods of time maybe even years
claims.claim: Sectors are traded only when a supply-demand story gives an attractive risk-reward, and can sit idle for years.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: I remember Goldman Sachs talking you know 200 bucks a barrel and and then we get the innovation of shale
claims.claim: Oil forecasts at $150-200 in 2007-08 extrapolated scarcity, but shale innovation added supply, so commodity cycles end by innovation.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: So commodities I think are quite disappointing in respect to constantly moving upwards
claims.claim: Commodities are cyclical and do not trend upward over the long run because innovation and substitution cap prices.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: 20 years later and we're at similar pricing because of you know the innovations and substitutions
claims.claim: Oil broke $50 in 2005 and is near $55 in late 2025 because shale added about 9 million barrels a day in 15 years.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: any sort of weather you get, it seems around the world today just doesn't affect what's uh these great seeds
claims.claim: GMO seeds make grain output resilient to weather, so food supply grows beyond population trend without a land grab, capping grain price spikes.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we do think that that you know base metals your copper aluminium lithium this is not so straightforward maybe to find different production areas or to or to manage demand so easily
claims.claim: Fund is pivoting to electrification metals (copper, aluminium, lithium) because supply and demand are harder to adjust, while other commodities look well supplied.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: all these passive index you know funds petting their wares and you know it's like really that's how you lose all your money
claims.claim: Passive commodity index funds and ETFs lose money; USO and UNG with a static roll lost everything, USO especially when WTI went negative.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: if you trying to go that granular, you're going to miss loads of stuff out of the situation
claims.claim: Tracking ships and tank tops is too granular; deep supply-demand work and demand stress tests matter more.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: all the major trading houses use physical really to then leverage paper
claims.claim: Trading houses use physical information to trade leveraged derivatives, which produced large profits in 2021-22 distortions.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we really wanted to see how much was there to be given uh at the expir the expiry point
claims.claim: The fund took physical delivery (rubber, raw sugar) to check whether scarcity was real before staying bullish.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we will have rocket ship moments where distortions come and that's you've got to be in it. Don't try and second guess when they occur because you won't be able to do that and you'll come late
claims.claim: Be positioned for rare commodity distortions in advance and earn a decent return in quiet years, since entering after the move means being late.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we would probably have somewhere between five and 20 strategies. We'd probably have two or three themes, maybe four
claims.claim: Portfolio holds 5-20 strategies in 2-4 themes with limits per theme, concentrated but not all-in on one.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: So we don't want to be wasting any of our risk bullets in there
claims.claim: Risk is held back from sectors without a supply-demand story, such as grains in 2017-2019, when they were well supplied at full carry.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: draw down of risk budget um further draw down of risk budget and then full draw down of risk budget and out
claims.claim: Positions are cut in stages as the risk budget is drawn down, then closed and sidelined for a period.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we target V in our hedge fund of around 21% annualized V
claims.claim: The fund targets about 21% annualised volatility and runs at no more than half of that when out of step with markets after drawdown.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: for us losing money is very poor because we have to grind it back rather than shoot it back with the target V that we would like to work with
claims.claim: Cutting the volatility target after a loss slows recovery, so losses are especially costly.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: when we have high vol in our strategies that that isn't ideal for us just because we can't maintain positions with that V very easily with our risk process
claims.claim: Under volatility targeting, spikes (cocoa, coffee, WTI negative) force position cuts so the fund cannot hold full size on big moves.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: a large part of the final move of that will be margin call stress and that isn't real that's financial stress
claims.claim: The last part of a cocoa or coffee spike is margin-call stress, not fundamentals, so the key is cash valuation and what people are really doing.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: if you had a short position and it's now costing you 20% more to hold on the exchange um some let it go the next day and that just squeezes the market even higher
claims.claim: Exchange margin hikes (ICE cocoa) force shorts to cover, which squeezes prices; long-standing cotton hedgers were also wiped out by margin calls.

correction.issue: Merges two speakers: the ICE cocoa margin-hike squeeze is Seibert's point, while the cotton merchants wiped out by margin calls is King's story (added separately as MT043-C07-X1).
correction.fix: Seibert: when ICE raised cocoa margin requirements near the highs, shorts facing a ~20% higher holding cost covered the next day, squeezing the price higher.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: they had way too low limits and so you'd be lot limit gone uh lot limit gone lot limit gone and it wasn't even a big move
claims.claim: In 2007-2009 low price limits made ag futures untradable and drove trading to an opaque synthetic options market, causing blow-ups.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: If the solution is flat price, it means that the price is in our view too low or too high and needs to correct to rebalance the supply and demand
claims.claim: Outright trades are used when price is too high or low for supply-demand balance, otherwise the right structure is a spread.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: it's not really a flat price curve it's a you flat price trade it's a it's a curve trade
claims.claim: Temporary scarcity or surplus (Covid oversupply into storage) is traded through curve spreads, not flat price.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: some of the best trades that we've had have been relative value trades where especially let's say a full carry where you can leverage very highly on on a on a very low downside trade
claims.claim: Best trades were leveraged curve trades at full carry: low downside because storage is full, with a flip from carry to inverse as OPEC cuts or demand rises.
claims.direction: Long front vs back when curve flips

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we felt that the shale growth year on year on year in the states was just eating OPEC's pie
claims.claim: The 2014 bearish oil view combined shale supply growth taking OPEC share with a global GDP slowdown (1-2% not 3-4%), expecting inverse to contango.
claims.indicator: US shale output; global GDP growth

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we quickly got out of that position
claims.claim: Fund cut the oil short when ISIS risk emerged in Iraq, and re-entered once the thesis held.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we came back in uh quite aggressively in in I think July August
claims.claim: After the Iraq shock, adding back to the short was right: global growth disappointed and surpluses built.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: So we went from about 120 to about 40 in five months and we I think we made 60% on the year
claims.claim: An OPEC price war accelerated the oil fall from about 120 to 40 in five months in 2014, giving about 60% for the fund.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: doing our own thing um and and not following sort of general, you know, situations
claims.claim: Independent positioning against the crowd, such as being bearish at peak oil sentiment, is the right approach.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: I think it was up 100% on that morning. So I did liquidate pretty much everything and then obviously was shocked when the futures exchange decided that they would not honor the futures trade
claims.claim: In the LME nickel squeeze the exchange cancelled trades after the market opened, so exchange intervention risk exists in extreme squeezes.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: the physical knowledge we were getting from that business was helpful for our derivative positioning within the hedge fund
claims.claim: A physical trading arm fed information into the hedge fund (like Cargill/Black River, Trafigura/Galena) but proved hard to run and was disbanded.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: credit exposure to a lot of countries where we were shipping product was high
claims.claim: Physical trading in 2014-17 had poor margins and high counterparty credit risk, which makes it less attractive than futures.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: if you're a fundamental trader cash information is critical. We look really really closely at basis, you know, the spread between cash and futures
claims.claim: Cash-futures basis is the key input for fundamental commodity traders.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: we talk to people in physical. We we don't talk to the derivative industry
claims.claim: Information comes from physical market participants, not from derivative sellers.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: the key thing in trading is what's your filter. What's relevant? What's not relevant is the key aspect of any very good trader is the noise removal
claims.claim: Edge in trading is filtering relevant from irrelevant information.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: they may be talking their book and not necessarily give the information that is objectively right
claims.claim: Fellow traders talk their book, so their views are weighted against physical facts.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: the cash market hasn't really moved. The basis has puked has has has fallen massively. It's just a demand for futures
claims.claim: In 2024 copper rose to $11,000 on futures demand without a cash basis follow-through, so the fund stayed out and the price fell to $9,000 six months later.

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: you have to derisk and then you have to re-risk and then you have to derisk
claims.claim: Global risk-off days (Liberation Day) force de-risking even when the commodity story is strong, repeatedly cutting and rebuilding positions.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: you have Henry up really not much happening then LG because of the Ukraine war and you know Europe needing that gas competing with competing with China for it um driving up the price
claims.claim: Regional gas prices can decouple: US Henry Hub stayed quiet while LNG prices rose because the Ukraine war made Europe compete with China for cargoes.
claims.direction: LNG up relative to Henry Hub
claims.conditions: European supply shock with competing Asian demand
claims.testable: yes - Henry Hub vs TTF/JKM spread history

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: they're buying physical and they're hedging futures until they can unwind it the other way. um and they are driven into huge margin core futures short explosions that end the business of a 130year merchant
claims.claim: Physical merchants who buy the commodity and hedge with short futures can be destroyed by margin calls in a futures short squeeze even though their book is hedged, as happened to a 130-year-old cotton merchant.
claims.indicator: futures margin calls on hedgers' short positions
claims.direction: squeeze pushes futures up and forces hedgers out
claims.conditions: sharp futures spikes with rising margin requirements
claims.testable: partly - squeeze episodes vs commercial short positioning (COT)

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: you could also see this [L380] that they bailed somebody else out who had the other positions
claims.claim: When an exchange cancels trades in a squeeze (LME nickel 2022), the stated reason is protecting the clearing house, but the effect is to bail out the distressed side at the expense of those who traded.
claims.indicator: exchange trade cancellations / rule changes in squeezes

claims.speaker: Doug King
claims.quote: if you fail two, three times, you'll be out the door in three months, six months, whatever
claims.claim: Multi-manager platforms run commodity PMs on very tight drawdown leashes (out after a few failures within months), unlike a single-team fund that can sit through noise around a long-term supply-demand theme.
